articleTitle: Design of a Prescription Management and Medication Availability Checking Web Application for Zimbabwe Using NLP and Database Querying
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: The increasing digitalisation of healthcare requires the development of secure and efficient systems for the management of medical prescriptions. This paper presents the design of a web-based application that enables physicians to securely send prescriptions following patient consultations. The design includes a Natural Language Processing (NLP) engine that is specifically trained to extract important information from these prescriptions, such as drug names, dosages and quantities. The design describes how the application will connect to multiple pharmacy databases via APIs or direct queries to provide real-time information on drug availability and pricing. This integration ensures that prescriptions are not only processed correctly but also checked against the latest inventory data. The proposed system architecture has been designed with security, efficiency and scalability in mind, making it suitable for use in a wide range of healthcare facilities. The paper describes the technical architecture, including data flow, component interaction, and the rationale for the NLP algorithms and database connection methods chosen. The proposed system design will significantly improve the accuracy and speed of prescription processing, underlining its potential as a valuable tool in modern healthcare

articleTitle: Allergen-Aware Food Ordering Web App for a Fast Food Restaurant
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: This study focuses on the development and implementation of a system designed to detect allergens in food ingredients using Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques. The system was created to improve food safety and prevent allergic reactions by accurately identifying allergens found in product ingredients. Python, Flask, and MySQL were used to create the system, which detects allergens using natural language processing (NLP) techniques. The methodology involved tokenising input text, removing stop words, lemmatization and matching tokens against a database of known allergens. The results show that the system detects allergens with high accuracy while also providing a more user- friendly and accessible interface for end users, which compares favourably to existing literature. The system's implementation provides a valuable tool for people with food allergies, allowing them to make safer food choices and potentially lower their risk of allergic reactions.

articleTitle: Rural-Based Agricultural Ecommerce Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: This project aimed to design and implement a rural-based agricultural e-commerce platform in Zimbabwe, addressing the longstanding challenges faced by rural farmers in accessing markets, achieving fair pricing, and overcoming logistical hurdles. Through a user-centred design approach and collaborative stakeholder engagement, the platform was developed to connect rural farmers directly with consumers and broader markets. Key features include enhanced market access, improved pricing, a user-friendly interface, logistics integration, and training programs for farmers. The platform has demonstrated significant potential in transforming the agricultural sector, improving livelihoods, and contributing to economic development goals in Zimbabwe. This project documentation provides a comprehensive overview of the project's objectives, methodology, achievements, challenges, and recommendations for future work, serving as a valuable resource for stakeholders and researchers in the field of agricultural e-commerce and rural development.

articleTitle: The use of Handheld Devices to Enhance Teaching and Learning in Nursing and Midwifery Education: Research-in-Progress Paper
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: The study aims to explore the integration of handheld devices in nursing and midwifery education, assessing pedagogical factors and their impact on self-regulated learning and digital application. It also examines the technological factors affecting this integration and the relationship between technological and pedagogical factors. The study also evaluates the role of handheld device integration in professional development. The Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) are used for this study. Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) is the tool to test the hypothesis. A cross-sectional survey is used to determine the best ways to integrate handheld devices into nursing education, with data collected from 335 students and 20 educators using multistage and purposive sampling strategies. The study contributes to the body of knowledge on emerging smart technology in low- and middle-income nations.

articleTitle: A Preliminary Framework for Optimising Test Case Selection Using Natural Language Processing and Test Case Prioritisation Using Deep Learning in Continuous Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: Regression testing, though crucial for software quality, is extremely time consuming especially in continuous integration environments. Test case prioritisation can however improve the efficiency of this process by re-ordering test execution. However, due to the growing volume of test cases in continuous integration, effective selection and prioritisation of test cases is a noteworthy challenge. This paper focusses on improving test case selection and test case prioritisation for regression testing in dynamic continuous integration environments. By applying natural language processing to semantically analyse test cases to include implicit test cases in testing, and deep learning to prioritise the most impactful test cases, this approach will reduce the time and resources required for regression testing while maintaining high fault detection and feedback transmission rates. This early stage research paper proposes a new conceptual framework for optimising regression testing in continuous integration environments using natural language processing and deep learning and outlines potential challenges and future research. The expected outcomes of this proposed framework include improved fault detection rates, reduced overall testing time, and improved resource utilisation. The effectiveness of the framework will be evaluated using metrics such as fault detection rate, testing cycle duration, and computational resource efficiency, providing a comprehensive assessment of its impact on software quality assurance.

articleTitle: Krispy: Empowering Sellers and Shoppers in a Digital Marketplace
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: This paper focuses on web development and the Zimbabwean Online Marketplace. The Zimbabwean e-commerce sector faces significant challenges due to fragmented platforms and lack of access to popular social media shopping tools, leading to decreased customer satisfaction and reliance on foreign markets. Krispy addresses these issues by providing a comprehensive, user-friendly platform that supports local businesses, enhances the shopping experience, and integrates crucial third-party services. Key achievements include the development of a functional multi-vendor platform, user-centric interface, seamless third-party integration, and thorough evaluation to ensure functionality, performance, and user satisfaction. There is improved product discoverability. This paper significantly contributes to the growth of Zimbabwean businesses and the economy by offering a unified digital marketplace that fosters collaboration, innovation, and customer satisfaction.

articleTitle: Adoption, Barriers, and Scaling Opportunities of Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things in the Zimbabwean Food Manufacturing Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: The adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the Internet of Things (IoT) offers significant opportunities to enhance competitiveness, efficiency, and sustainability in Zimbabwe's food manufacturing sector amid the global shift towards the Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR). However, the adoption rate of these technologies remains low. This study examines the current state of AI and IoT adoption in Zimbabwe's food manufacturing sector, identifies key barriers hindering their implementation, and proposes scalable solutions. Using a mixed-methods approach that combines descriptive and explanatory designs, this research collected data through a semi-structured survey and analysed it using descriptive statistics, binomial logistic regression and exploratory factor analysis (EFA) in R (R Core Team, 2023). The study found that AI and IoT adoption in food manufacturing was 16.7% (95% Confidence Interval [CI]: 9.0% - 28.3%). These findings also revealed that company size is not a significant predictor of AI adoption, indicating that other factors are more influential. Key barriers identified were categorised into organisational and data challenges, technical and financial challenges, and leadership and regulation challenges. The most significant obstacles are insufficient data for training, lack of key skills, high costs of implementation, and infrastructural deficiencies. The study proposes a multifaceted strategy to scale AI and IoT adoption, such as integration of the technologies into industry certifications, public-private partnerships with the government on policy development, and developing adaptable technology solutions. The study also emphasises leveraging industry expertise, fostering organisational buy-in, and providing comprehensive employee training to overcome barriers. It also highlights the need for ongoing investment, research and innovation to address the complexities of adopting scalable technology solutions tailored to local needs.

articleTitle: Exploring the Cybersecurity Measures Implemented by Internet Service Providers (ISPs) to Mitigate Cyberthreats: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: The occurrence and severity of cyberthreats have surged substantially, leading to damage to individuals, organizations, and society. Internet Service Providers (ISPs) play a crucial role in defending threats through their expertise and robust infrastructure, offering proactive security measures as a vital line of defence. However, emerging technologies and trends like cloud services, mobile apps, and remote work created new vulnerabilities that cyberthreats can exploit. This requires additional security measures to mitigate the risks. This paper presents results of a systematic literature review that explored strategies for ISPs to help mitigate cybersecurity threats. The review found a comprehensive approach combining people, technology, and adherence to regulations. The study has implications for policymakers, who need to ensure relevant policies are in place, and for software/hardware vendors, who should incorporate appropriate countermeasures into system designs. ISPs also have an obligation to allocate sufficient funding to cybersecurity measures to protect organizational and individual data.

articleTitle: Blockchain-Enhanced Cloud Security for Zimbabwean Educational Institutions: A Case Study of NUST's Hybrid Infrastructure
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: This study examined how blockchain technology can improve cloud security for educational institutions in Zimbabwe, using the National University of Science and Technology as a case study. This brought us to our primary research question, which aims to answer how NUST's cloud-based systems can be secure, and private, and enhance integrity by including blockchain technology. This research aims to aid in academic value, as it offers a new hybrid-cloud structure for protecting sensitive data at a time when cyber-attacks continue to rise. The research methods involved a critical review of the literature, an analysis of the current architecture at NUST, and the development and testing of the secure UniBlockNet model. The primary findings demonstrate improvements in data security, immutability, and transparency; there was a 42% increase in audit trail accuracy and a 37% drop in illegal access attempts. It is therefore advised to develop a phased adoption plan to address implementation costs and scale. Some important contributions of this paper are the designing and implementation of an augmented blockchain security framework for Zimbabwean educational institutions and a few practice-based recommendations including, training the staff and policy changes. For this, the methodology used a mixture of quantitative and qualitative approaches, which included security policy review, network topology mapping, and vulnerability assessment. The study concluded that blockchain technology can go far in enhancing cloud security within educational environments, therefore laying the foundation for more resilient digital infrastructure and securing electronic systems operation in the academic sector in Zimbabwe.

articleTitle: Internet Penetration and Social Media Usage in the SADC Region: *Note: Sub-Titles are not Captured in Xplore and Should not be Used
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: Africa has a lot of economic opportunities that exist in various sectors. Much of the population is very youthful and must take advantage of opportunities brought about by digital transformation and internet penetration in the continent to make digitally enabled socio-economic development a high priority. For an innovative, inclusive and sustainable growth, Africa should embrace Digital Transformation as a driving force. This will help in reducing poverty and inequality, thereby allowing creating goods and services, that will help the continent in achieving its goals in the Agenda 2063 and the Sustainable Development Goals. African leaders need to prioritize the acceleration of digital transformation so that their countries can have a comprehensive strategy so that they can have a common, coordinated plan for them to reap the benefits of the fourth industrial revolution. In this paper we conduct desk research to ascertain the level of Internet penetration in the SADC regional block of Africa. The results show that in most SADC countries, the majority of the people live in rural areas except for South Africa, Seychelles and Namibia who have 31.7%, 41.6% and 46.2% rural populations, respectively. Internet penetration in most SADC countries is still less than 50% of the population except for Botswana, Lesotho, Mauritius, Namibia, Seychelles and South Africa, who had more than 50% of the population with Internet connection. Mobile phones have become a central part of people's lives and have a great economic importance since most people in the SADC region use their phones for financial transactions. In all countries, the number of mobile connections were more than 100%, except in Angola, Comoros, Madagascar, Malawi and Mozambique. This substantial number can be attributed to the fact that a lot of people in all corners of the world use at least one mobile connection. These Internet connections may either be, for example, one for work and the other for personal use. So, it is expected for figures of the mobile connections to rise depending on the population. The research also looked at the use of social media as a measure of use of Internet in the population. The social media looked at were Facebook, Instagram, Facebook messenger, LinkedIn, and Twitter. In the whole of SADC countries, only Mauritius and Seychelles had more than 50% of the population using social media, with 78.6% and 74%, respectively. We also collected data on the percentage of the population with mobile connection. From the research we concluded that, in most SADC countries, more effort is still required to bridge the digital divide. There is need for more people to be afforded the chance to have an Internet connection by providing financial opportunities for citizens to buy mobile phones and to have a fixed Internet connection. Governments should make policies that will encourage the use of ICT for social-economic development of the continent towards attaining Agenda 2063 and the Sustainable development goals.

articleTitle: Monitoring Tobacco Crop Health using Geospatial Data
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: This study examines a method that uses the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) to track the health of tobacco crops and provide farmers practical advice. The NDVI was calculated using Sentinel-2 and Landsat satellite image data. Google Earth Engine (GEE) was used to process the images. The method demonstrated a 91.7% accuracy in categorising crops, and a very small mean absolute error of 0.02 in NDVI computation. Nevertheless, drawbacks were observed, including the limits of a rule-based recommendation system, possible spectrum misinterpretation, and data gaps under foggy situations. Comparative field tests conducted over a month showed a 91.25% agreement between the system's suggestions and actual results. Future research is advised to incorporate other data sources, such as Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR), improve data imputation methods, and switch to a dynamic recommendation model. The results show the system's potential as a scalable tool for precision agriculture. This means the system can empower farmers with timely insights to optimise crop management, reduce costs, and improve productivity.

articleTitle: Assessing Computer-Based Clinical Decision Support in Healthcare: Research-in-Progress Paper
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: In healthcare, the integration of Computer-Based Clinical Decision Support Systems (CDSS) is increasingly recognized as a critical factor in improving clinical decision-making and patient outcomes. However, the successful implementation of CDSS is often hindered by challenges related to system quality, service quality, and integration into clinical workflows. This study investigates the role of Computer-based CDSS affects overall healthcare delivery, including improvements in processes, patient outcomes, and integration within the healthcare system within the specific context of hospitals and clinics in Ghana. The research employs a mixed-methods approach, combining quantitative surveys and qualitative interviews to explore the perceptions and experiences of healthcare providers and patients using CDSS. The DeLone & McLean Information Systems Success Model serves as the theoretical framework, with a focus on extending the constructs of System Quality and Service Quality to encompass factors such as interoperability, clinical workflow integration, data security, and organizational support. As a work in progress, this study is expected to contribute to both the theoretical understanding and practical application of CDSS in healthcare. The preliminary findings aims to provide new insights into how CDSS can be optimized to enhance clinical decision-making processes and improve healthcare delivery in Ghana. The findings will inform healthcare practitioners and policymakers about best practices for implementing and utilizing CDSS, with the goal of advancing the quality of care and patient outcomes.

articleTitle: Multilingual Conversational AI Framework for Empowering Maternal and Child Healthcare in Zimbabwe
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: The purpose of this study was to examine the potential benefits of a multilingual conversational AI framework for mother and child healthcare in Zimbabwe. This country has language hurdles towards healthcare access. By creating an artificial intelligence (AI) system that can understand Shona, Ndebele, and English, the research hopes to reduce communication gaps for linguistically varied communities. The study employed a mixed-methods approach, integrating both quantitative analysis of AI-patient dialogues and qualitative interviews with healthcare experts. ZimHealthBERT (a novel modification of BERT architecture), an AI model, was developed with transformer-based architectures, and a medical knowledge graph to ensure that responses were correct and suitable for a given culture. It also included cultural adaption layers. This model was trained online using the NVIDIA A100 GPU on RunPod Console. According to key results, prenatal care attendance increased by 21.9%, medication adherence increased by 20.6%, and patient comprehension improved by 35.5%. Healthcare workers reported 68.7% less time devoted to interpreting languages and a 30.9% increase in efficiency. In comparison to human interpreters, the research demonstrates greater management of culturally sensitive topics by providing a multilingual AI system specifically designed for African healthcare facilities. This represents cutting-edge contributions. The results demonstrate this framework's capacity to lessen healthcare disparities and imply that it can be expanded to additional multilingual developing countries. Future research will examine how to improve the system's accessibility in remote places through offline functionality, more cultural adaption enhancements, and possible integration with telemedicine platforms.

articleTitle: Design of a Model for Integrating Digital Forensics into Information System Auditing in the Financial Sector
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: Integrating digital forensics into Information Systems (IS) audits has become increasingly crucial in the financial sector, where ensuring data confidentiality, integrity, and availability (CIA) is paramount. This study aimed to develop a model that seamlessly incorporates digital forensics into the IS audit process, ensuring compliance with organizational policies, industry standards, and legal requirements. Using a Design Science Research (DSR) methodology, supported by a literature review, the research identified key gaps in traditional evidencegathering techniques within the financial industry. The proposed model was iteratively designed and evaluated to address these deficiencies. By incorporating forensic methods, the model enhances the reliability of audit evidence, mitigating risks related to internal control weaknesses, fraud, and cyber threats. This approach ultimately strengthens the integrity and accuracy of IS audits, safeguarding financial data from potential discrepancies.

articleTitle: Broadband Network Simulations Towards Cost Assessments: Case of a Namibian Rural Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: Broadband connection has gradually become a vital component of communities, particularly in rural regions. Access to services, particularly in healthcare, is critical, and the internet may significantly facilitate related services, specifically telehealth. Video connections among healthcare practitioners for medical services may become a reality in remote areas. Broadband network alternatives encompass Television Whitespaces (TVWS). The issue, however, is that telehealth services cannot be sufficiently supported in rural hospitals due to restricted broadband internet connection resulting from expenses. This study aimed to address the research hypothesis, “The deployment of TVWS networks are cost effective when compared to fixed LTE in the Kunene region, for rural healthcare services”. A positivist paradigm was utilized in the study's approach. This paradigm supports experimental designs. Network simulation experiments were conducted in testing the study's hypothesis. A rural setting in the Kunene region was selected as the study area for this research. The data collection methods included simulations. Data analysis involved simulations of TVWS and fixed LTE broadband networks, from which the necessary infrastructure mapping was derived. Network standards, particularly those for high-performance networks, were deemed essential for facilitating telehealth application connections in rural regions. Cost assessments were carried out based on the simulations and network infrastructure requirements (technical design). This paper conducted network simulations towards network performance and cost assessment as outcomes.

articleTitle: Tamper-Resistant Document Management System Integrated with Blockchain Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: This paper focuses on the development of a Tamper-Resistant Document Management System integrated with blockchain technology to create tamper-proof records of document interactions. A tamper-resistant Document Management System integrated with blockchain technology was developed to address the challenges of document security, integrity, and traceability in modern business environments. The system was designed for organisations and businesses in Zimbabwe that handle sensitive information and require robust document management solutions. This includes government agencies, financial institutions, healthcare providers, educational institutions, legal firms, and non-governmental organisations. The paper was motivated by the need to mitigate the risks of unauthorised access, data breaches, and document tampering, which can lead to costly errors, productivity losses, and compromised client relations. The system successfully achieved its objectives, demonstrating enhanced security, transparency, and immutability in document management. It provides a single authenticated platform that creates an immutable record for each file handled, ensuring tamper-proof records of document interactions. The results align with existing literature on the benefits of blockchain technology in document management, particularly in enhancing security, transparency, and trust. The system's use of a centralised repository with blockchain integration for verification aligns with current trends in balancing centralised and decentralised approaches. The system offers significant benefits to its target users by improving the efficiency and security of document management. It helps mitigate risks such as security breaches, costly errors, productivity losses, and compromised client relations. Additionally, it provides valuable insights into the significance of proper document-handling practices in modern business environments.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Analysis of Types, Functional Goals and Usability Factors of WhatsApp Chatbots Implemented in Zimbabwe
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: Chatbots are increasingly becoming prevalent across digital platforms. Among these digital platforms, WhatsApp has emerged as a popular medium for deploying chatbots due to its widespread adoption and user accessibility. However, research gaps persist, particularly regarding the implementation and effectiveness of WhatsApp chatbots in developing economies like Zimbabwe. This study provides a comprehensive analysis of WhatsApp chatbots adoption in Zimbabwe, focusing on the different types of chatbots that exist, their functional goals and usability factors. The research employs a pragmatic approach, integrating qualitative and quantitative methods to address key questions about the types, functional goals, and usability issues of WhatsApp chatbots in Zimbabwean companies. Through a mixed methods strategy, including case studies and usability assessments, the study identifies active chatbots, categorises their functional goals and evaluates their usability attributes such as response speed and context switching flexibility. Findings reveal a predominance of rule-based chatbots with limited contextual flexibility and language support in Zimbabwe. The study recommends the improvement of chatbots design for enhanced usability and multilingual support to broaden accessibility. Moreover, the study proposes the development of domain-specific natural language processing models and usability assessment frameworks to optimise WhatsApp chatbot adoption in Zimbabwe and similar contexts.

articleTitle: Conversational Commerce: Designing and Evaluating a Whatsapp-Based e-Commerce Chatbot
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: This paper presents the design, development, and comprehensive evaluation of an advanced WhatsApp-based e-commerce chatbot. By integrating product search, secure payment processing, and order fulfilment functionalities within the WhatsApp platform, the system enhances the customer experience through Natural Language Processing (NLP) and machine learning techniques. The chatbot demonstrated significant improvements in user engagement, transaction completion rates, and operational cost reductions. Initial experiments show high user satisfaction with a 97% success rate in catalogue navigation and a 95% transaction completion rate. Future improvements will focus on multi-language support, AI-driven recommendations, and enhanced payment options.

articleTitle: Exploring and Preprocessing of Crunchbase Data for Accurate Startup Success Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: Startups are the backbone of the country's economy. The growth of startups is supporting the country by providing jobs and also directly generating revenue for the government. On the other hand, the failure of startups is impacting the economy's growth. Therefore, we need to explore and study the factors of startup success and failure. However, there is very fewer source of information about the startup's activity available openly, but the databases like Crunchbase are collecting and providing data about the startups for conducting study. In this paper, we are focusing on Crunchbase data for exploring the essential facts and attributes which are significantly contributing to startup success and failure. Additionally, we also proposed a machine learning model to accurately predict startup success and failure by utilizing the concluded attributes. The aim of the proposed model is to identify how the funding influences the operational status of the company. Thus, the Crunchbase dataset is considered where 66368 companies' data are used for evaluation and experiment. According to the conducted experiments we have found that venture capital financing is the main source of getting funds, 63.99% of companies are able to secure only the first round of funding, and less than 1 % of companies are able to get funding more than 10 times. The combination of the proposed preprocessing technique and learning algorithms provides highly accurate results and is able to predict 80% success and failure.

articleTitle: Enhancing IoT Security for Socio-Economic Development in the Mirror of Challenges, Emerging Technologies, and Holistic Solutions
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is rapidly transforming sectors like healthcare, agriculture, and disaster management, particularly in developing regions. However, its widespread adoption in Africa is hindered by security vulnerabilities, infrastructure deficits, and socio-economic barriers, particularly in rural areas. This study investigates these challenges and explores the potential of integrating technologies such as machine learning, blockchain, and edge computing to mitigate security risks. While these technologies offer promising solutions, they introduce additional complexities that must be carefully managed. A systematic approach to reviewing and analyzing the literature on emerging technologies, particularly the Internet of Things (IoT), and their socio-economic impact in developing regions is adopted. The research emphasizes the need for inclusive, context-specific strategies, particularly in addressing the digital divide and improving digital literacy, which remain critical obstacles in rural areas. Lightweight, cost-effective security measures, coupled with investment in digital infrastructure and capacitybuilding, are vital to advancing IoT adoption. The study further underscores the importance of comprehensive regulatory frameworks and fostering public-private partnerships to ensure the scalable and secure deployment of IoT systems. By addressing both technological and socio-economic challenges, policymakers and practitioners can unlock IoT's full potential, contributing to sustainable development and transformative change in key sectors. The findings call for ongoing collaboration between governments, industries, and international partners to create an enabling environment for innovation, security, and inclusivity in Africa's IoT landscape.

articleTitle: Information Security Culture: The Effect of Strategy, Technology, Organization, People and the Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: Financial services organizations are one of the leading targets of information security infringements because of the potential of the assailants to reap financial rewards from launching the attacks. Information security culture which is a collection of socio-cultural procedures implemented by firms, is predicted to forestall the menace of information security breaches. Information security culture targets to protect the information assets of firms through influencing personnel to conduct themselves in a way that is well-suited to the protection of firms' assets. Information security strategy, technology, organisation, people and environment are proposed as some of the main determinants of information security culture in the financial services. Therefore, this paper investigates the impact that strategy, technology, organisation, people and environment exert on financial services firms' information security culture. This paper is a quantitative case study of four financial services firms in Zimbabwe. The results of this study show that strategy, technology and environment are predictors of information security culture in the financial services. Conversely, the study established that, organisation, people are not related to information security culture in the financial services.

articleTitle: Implementation of Telemedicine in Zimbabwe's Remote Areas: Guidelines for its Success
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: Telemedicine offers a transformative solution to the healthcare challenges faced by Zimbabwe, particularly in remote areas with limited access to medical professionals and facilities. The study aimed to develop practical recommendations for the successful implementation of telemedicine technologies to enhance access to healthcare services in remote and underserved areas. The guidelines were developed through a comprehensive literature review, expert consultation, and field research from Zimbabwe's 5 provinces. The study identified key factors that can affect the implementation of telemedicine, including technological infrastructure, regulatory frameworks, and training and support for healthcare providers. The guidelines provide specific recommendations on these factors, highlighting the importance of engaging local communities, building sustainable partnerships, and ensuring the confidentiality and security of patient data. The successful implementation of telemedicine in remote areas requires a coordinated effort between healthcare providers, policymakers, and technology experts. The guidelines can serve as a valuable resource for stakeholders involved in the planning and implementation of telemedicine initiatives in remote areas of Zimbabwe and other low-resource settings.

articleTitle: Building a Peer-to-Peer Learning Platform for University Students Using WebRTC and Mobile Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: In South Africa, pursuing a university degree can be a challenging prospect, with the approach to learning and the type of communication between students and teachers changing, as compared to secondary school level. It comes as no surprise that most first-year students tend to struggle at university level. This is especially true for students who come from disadvantaged backgrounds. These students tend to come from schools that fail to equip them with the necessary skills required to master basic concepts taught in university. These students usually have little to no experience in using computers, which significantly hampers their chances of graduation. This results in some students not engaging with the learning materials or participating in course-related activities. Although the tools for assisting these students already exist, they limit students in what they can contribute and benefit from the learning process and do little to aid collaboration among students. With university resources being stretched and demands on academic staff increasing every year, universities cannot be expected to solve these problems entirely. If appropriately applied, peer-to-peer learning could provide an affordable and easily scalable solution to this problem. In following the design science research methodology, this study uses mobile technology and Web Real Time Communications (WebRTC) to build an online peer-to-peer learning platform for first-year students in order to increase engagement with course content, interaction with the teachers and student collaboration. The platform could provide an affordable solution to a very expensive problem if it achieves its objectives.

articleTitle: Bridging the Digital Divide by Advancing Education 5.0 Through E-Learning Innovations in Resource-Constrained Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: The authors critically examine the integration of e-learning systems in advancing Education 5.0 within developing contexts, focusing on Zimbabwe's higher education sector. This qualitative enquiry, grounded in the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and Constructivist Learning Theory, explores how e-learning can be operationalised to meet the objectives of Education 5.0. Data from 18 key informant interviews and a 10-member focus group provided insights into the technological and pedagogical innovations necessary for aligning digital education with Education 5.0's goals. Findings highlight significant barriers, including inadequate infrastructure and resistance to change, and propose a reimagined, context-specific e-learning model designed to foster engagement, innovation, and graduate readiness. The study underscores the urgent need for strategic investment in digital infrastructure and the redesign of pedagogical approaches to harness the potential of e-learning for socio-economic development in resource-constrained environments.

articleTitle: Transforming Chartered Governance Through AI and Big Data
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: This study investigates the transformative integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Big Data into chartered governance, bridging the gap between traditional governance practices and the potential of these advanced technologies. Employing a qualitative methodology with semistructured interviews of 20 governance professionals, the research explores benefits, challenges and ethical considerations. The findings reveal significant enhancements in efficiency, accuracy and decision-making, alongside barriers such as data privacy concerns, algorithmic complexity and skill gaps. This study extends theoretical frameworks including the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), Resource-Based View (RBV) and Institutional Theory, providing empirical insights into the interplay of technology, organisational strategies and regulatory demands. Practical recommendations include phased implementation, staff training, establishing ethics committees and fostering interdisciplinary collaboration. This study provides a foundation for future research to further explore the evolving integration of AI and Big Data in governance, addressing emerging trends and fostering innovation.

articleTitle: Electricity Theft Detection Machine-Learning Models for Windhoek Informal Settlements
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: Monitoring and managing resources for electricity distribution is a challenging task, as there are several ways in which revenue leakages may happen. As hardware equipment used in the electricity distribution gets worn out, it becomes inefficient, thus affecting the quality of electricity distributed. Such inherent and unavoidable losses are known as technical losses. Conversely, non-technical losses are man-made and result in direct income loss for electricity utilities through human errors or fraudulent actions. Examples include billing fraud, meter tempering, or illegal connections. This paper focuses on mitigating challenges that arose from non-technical challenges by using machine learning techniques to detect potential electricity theft. Historical electricity purchasing data of Goreangab and Havana clients from 2016 to 2022 was used to train K-means and Isolation Forest clustering algorithms. Early results of the trained models showed K-means clustering with a silhouette score of 0.711 and Isolation forest performing well under various contamination factors. Results also showed the potential of detecting electricity theft early at lower costs and shorter times than conventional monitoring means. Besides, most developing countries still need to install additional equipment for smart grids and usually resort to random meter inspections. Apart from such an alternative being far less precise because of the randomness, it is also costly in the long run as it requires resources to transport inspectors to the client's premises. As researchers, we are convinced that our solution can reduce revenue leakages for utility companies at a low cost with high precision if optimized.

articleTitle: Investigating the state of cyber-security awareness by Zimbabwean citizens
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: Connection to the internet is regarded a basic human right hence most Zimbabwean citizens have this privilege. This has resulted in almost every Zimbabwean citizen using social media, transact on line among other internet uses. However, there are concerns about the usage of this precious resource; cybercrime and cyber-security being the two major concerns. In 2017, the former president of Zimbabwe Robert Gabriel Mugabe introduced a Ministry of Cyber-security in Zimbabwe which many mocked and regarded as a political interest. This effort however showed the government's willingness to embrace a cyber-security culture in Zimbabwe. However currently in Zimbabwe, there is little to no documented policy that stipulates what cyber-security is let alone cybercrime. Though the country is operating in this status quo, cyber space in Zimbabwe like any other country has become a platform for different globalized criminal activities hence the need for cyber-security. Regardless of the government of Zimbabwe's efforts to enforce law which encourage a cybersecurity culture, its efforts for cyber-security awareness are far below what can be expected in a cyber-world. As a result, many cyber activities are inclined to cybercrime hence an indication of a lack in cyber-security awareness. Thus, the purpose of this paper was to investigate the state of cyber-security awareness in Zimbabwe. Data was gathered using 1250 random semistructured questionnaires administered in Zimbabwe's five cities. The results showed that Zimbabweans still have embryonic understanding for cyber-security issues.

articleTitle: Reducing Patient Waiting Time at Public Hospitals Through Predictive Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: Reducing patient waiting times in public hospitals is a critical challenge that significantly impacts patient satisfaction, healthcare outcomes, and operational efficiency. Efficient, effective, and timely patient care contributes toward patient service satisfaction. This is not always true for most healthcare institutions. This paper investigates the use of predictive modeling in addressing patient waiting time by leveraging historical data from electronic records at five selected public health centers in Harare, Bulawayo, and Gweru between October 1 and 31 December 2023. The objective was to identify a predictive model that could effectively classify the queue data into two categories: delayed (Yes) or not delayed (No). Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and XGBoost models were trained using Stratified K-Fold cross-validation to determine the model with the best fit on the original data. The models were trained using variables such as queue position, wait time, service time, location of the health center, and weekday as predictors. XGBoost emerged as the top model, achieving the highest ROC AUC of 0.63, compared to the other models which ranged from 0.56 to 0.6. The selected model was then evaluated using F1 Score, ROC Curve, and Precision-Recall Curve. Results showed a high F1 Score of 0.702, indicating the model's ability to distinguish between the positive (Delayed) and negative (Not Delayed) classes. The area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.63 further quantified the model's overall ability to discriminate between these classes. Additionally, the area under the Precision-Recall curve (AUC-PR) of 0.64 suggests that the model performs well in balancing precision and recall, effectively identifying most actual delayed services (high recall). Accurately predicting patient waiting times not only enhances patient care experience but also supports healthcare providers in delivering timely and efficient care. Designers of hospital programs can analyze patterns, and identify peak times, predict high-delay patient arrivals, and suggest real-time staffing adjustments. Future work will focus on refining the models and integrating them into hospital management systems for broader implementation.

articleTitle: AI - Driven Decision Support System for Optimizing Soil Analysis and Crop Management in Zimbabwe
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: Agricultural productivity among smallholder farmers in Zimbabwe is hindered by limited access to advanced soil management technologies and sustainable farming practices. This study presents the development of an AI-driven Decision Support System (AI-DSS) designed to optimize soil analysis and crop management, addressing these challenges through real-time, data-driven insights. The AI-DSS integrates soil sensor data, satellite imagery and local weather information to provide precise, actionable recommendations that improve soil health and crop yield. Using a mixed-methods approach, we combined qualitative insights from focus group discussions with quantitative data to enhance system usability and relevance for farmers. The model, based on Decision Trees and Neural Networks, achieved a 92% accuracy rate in diagnosing soil health, resulting in a 15% improvement in crop yields during field trials. This study contributes to sustainable agriculture in Zimbabwe by delivering a scalable, context-sensitive solution tailored to the specific needs of smallholder farmers. Our findings underscore the potential of AI-driven systems to transform resource-constrained farming, providing a model adaptable to similar agricultural settings globally.

articleTitle: A Systematic Review of Challenges and Opportunities in Integrating Big Data for Monitoring and Evaluation in Global Development Programmes
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: This systematic review explores the integration of Big Data into monitoring and evaluation (M&E) processes for global development programmes, highlighting key challenges and opportunities. This study followed the PRISMA guidelines for systematic reviews and searched Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, and PubMed, as well as development-focused databases such as the World Bank eLibrary and OECD iLibrary, and multidisciplinary sources like Google Scholar and ProQuest Central. A total of 30 studies met the final inclusion criteria. The review shows that Big Data offers significant potential to enhance M&E through real-time insights, improved decision-making, and the ability to identify patterns and trends that traditional methods may overlook. However, integrating Big Data presents several challenges, including concerns around data privacy and security, the digital divide, and the need for a skilled workforce to analyse complex data. This review synthesises existing literature to assess these challenges, and the opportunities Big Data provides for improving M&E processes. The findings underscore the need for supportive policy environments, enhanced data accessibility, and capacity building within organisations to fully leverage Big Data's potential. Recommendations for future research and practice are provided, focusing on enhancing data accessibility, improving privacy and security protocols, addressing the digital divide, and building the necessary capacity within organisations to leverage Big Data effectively in developmental M&E.

articleTitle: A Supervised Machine Learning Model for Predicting Adverse Drug Reactions Among Tuberculosis Patients in Zimbabwe
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: The paper develops a supervised machine learning model to predict adverse drug reactions (ADRs) among tuberculosis (TB) patients in Zimbabwe, addressing a critical need for tools that enhance patient safety and optimize treatment outcomes. The model integrates multimodal data, including chest X-ray images and patient-specific information, to provide comprehensive risk assessments. The study employs the Cross Industry Standard Process for Data Mining (CRISPDM) framework, using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to analyze X-rays and ensemble learning techniques to incorporate clinical data. The model achieved high predictive accuracy, with training accuracy reaching 95% and validation accuracy stabilizing at 78%. The confusion matrix analysis demonstrated the model's ability to differentiate between various severity levels of ADRs, facilitating targeted interventions. The research underscores the potential of machine learning in medical diagnostics, particularly in settings with limited resources and highlights the need for future research to refine the model using larger and more diverse datasets. The findings have significant implications for improving TB treatment and patient outcomes in Zimbabwe.

articleTitle: Assessment of Password Recovery Mechanisms on Electronic Learning Platforms
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: Most universities in Zimbabwe have changed the way they deliver education. A blended learning approach has become the norm, electronic learning platforms are complementing the traditional face-to-face interactions between students and lecturers. Though online platforms come along with several benefits, security concerns regarding student data exist. Passwords implemented might be forgotten, and to recover from this, password recovery mechanisms are used. Password recovery mechanisms implemented can introduce vulnerabilities and an attacker might recover a user's password by leveraging their loopholes. Therefore, this study seeks to assess the password recovery mechanisms used in electronic learning platforms of the selected universities in Zimbabwe. Additionally, the research uncovers flaws in password recovery processes and advises their implications on student data security. It is evident from the results that universities in Zimbabwe are using weak password recovery methods such as secret questions and email-based mechanisms. The research recommends coupling two or more password recovery mechanisms to improve security. Furthermore, in cases where budgets permit, the study recommends the use of stronger password recovery methods, such as multi device authentication and biometric based solutions.

articleTitle: Finding the Best Fit; Comparative Analysis of Supervised Learning Models for Student Feedback Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: This study developed a machine learning-based system to analyze student feedback on the quality of university courses, aiming to streamline the feedback process and enhance instructional delivery. Using a dataset collected from a Zimbabwean university Political Philosophy students, feedback was gathered through Google Forms, formatted as CSV files, and processed through Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques to clean and tokenize the text. Three machine learning models—Support Vector Machine (SVM), Logistic Regression (LR), and Multinomial Naive Bayes (MNB)—alongside deep learning models like BERT and CNN, were tested to identify the most effective classifier. SVM was selected after hyperparameter tuning, achieving a reliable 80% accuracy in sentiment classification. The final system generates a PDF-based Course Evaluation Summary Report that presents positive and negative feedback, key sentiment insights, and graphical summaries, offering instructors a clear, actionable overview of student perspectives. While deep learning models struggled with the dataset size, SVM proved optimal for small data contexts typical in university settings. Future work will focus on scaling the system with advanced NLP and larger datasets to broaden its applicability.

articleTitle: Review of a Zimbabwean Smart Connected Home System
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: In Zimbabwe, the upward thrust in housebreaking and robbery incidents has highlighted the pressing want for superior safety solutions. This have a look at aimed to deal with those issues with the aid of using growing a Smart Connected Home System that integrates diverse domestic automation technology to beautify safety and convenience. Recent literature underscores the effectiveness of IoT-primarily based totally structures and predictive algorithms in enhancing clever domestic functionality. Building on those advancements, this studies applied a machine that makes use of real-time alerts, faraway monitoring, and power control to provide complete safety and control. The proposed machine employs a mixture of real-time algorithms and fuzzy good judgment to reveal domestic environments, hit upon intrusions, and control utilities. Real-time algorithms, primarily based totally on IoT, allow instant responses to safety breaches and environmental changes. Meanwhile, fuzzy good judgment frameworks optimize power utilization with the aid of using adapting to variable inputs like sun and wind power, thereby improving each safety and efficiency. The technique concerned growing a prototype the use of Arduino-primarily based totally hardware, sensors for movement and fuel online detection, and a cell software for faraway control. Initial exams confirmed that the machine successfully video display units and controls domestic safety, presenting real-time notifications and automatic responses to capacity threats. The integration of predictive algorithms in addition subtle the machine's accuracy and efficiency.

articleTitle: Online Learning Modes and Learners' Safety Concerns in Zimbabwe's Marginalized Schools
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: Online learning has greatly influenced teaching and learning into interactive and collaborative approach. It is against this background that descriptive survey design was employed to gain an indepth insight on online learning implementation. Sample comprised 20 parents/guardians, 20 teachers and 15 secondary school students who were randomly selected. 5 I.T experts were purposively selected for the study. Semi-structured interviews and focus group discussions and online survey were administered. Descriptive statistics were used to analyse quantitative data while qualitative data was manually analyzed according to emerging themes. MLT and TAM formed the lens through which this study was observed. Findings revealed that online implementation was an important component in this information age in Zimbabwe as it facilitates ubiquitous learning environment. Findings also show that to a large extent stakeholders were not aware of online learning policies that govern learning activities. Furthermore, online activities showed some aspect of negative unhu/ubuntu in the community under study. Findings also revealed that integration of online learning face challenges such as lack of appropriate technological gadgets, exorbitant data and inappropriate technological knowledge and skills. Parent-teacher engagements during online learning activities were among strategies cited to reduce challenges. Therefore, the study recommended that training and workshops as well as designing systems that monitor learners online in learning institutions are an integral component in communities. The study suggests that further studies, which includes urban and rural location be carried so as to come up with an all-encompassing insight pertaining to best practices that enhance safety of learners online.
